notes: Short summary: Silverpine runs a multi-tenant support platform used by ~120 mid-market customers. They're piloting an embedded agent-assist + ticket summarization feature to reduce L2 handle time.

Key asks: reliable RAG with citations + freshness (hours); multi-source retrieval (Zendesk, Confluence, S3); deterministic tool-calling for account actions (close ticket, escalate); must handle 3x spike for seasonal events.
Quote from CTO: 'We need precise citations — agents must be able to see source paragraph + time stamp. If the model hallucinates a doc, we fail audits.'
Security: legal flagged EU residency for some clients; will require VPC + optional on-prem for certain customers. KMS integration mandatory for secrets at rest.
POC constraints: PII redaction pipeline must be deployed; team prefers Lightweight embeddings + reranker for speed. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization.
Performance target: average token cost sensitivity — mid-high; willing to trade cost for sub-400ms average latency on agent assist. Must maintain behavior under 3x baseline TPS.
Competitive signal: evaluating Replicant for end-to-end contact center automation and Ada for self-serve flows; Redwood's dedicated offering and RAG controls are differentiators.
Operational notes: SE will run synthetic spike test using 10k ticket queries; we will capture traces and share Console dashboard link post-run.
Typical sales shorthand used in CRM: 'RAG POC — ingest Zendesk + Confluence + S3; citation QA; stress test; SOC2 & residency ok?'
Drive artifacts stubbed: pricing proposal, security Q&A, POC checklist (see linked_drive_docs)
use_case_summary: Customer-facing agent-assist and summarization for support reps. Use RAG over multi-source KBs (Zendesk, Confluence, S3) to provide paragraph-level citations with timestamps; deterministic tool-calling to execute ticket workflows; guarantee latency and availability during traffic spikes. Need audit-friendly outputs, retention controls, and KMS-backed key management.
